# Abhisamaya Saṁyutta (SN 13)

**ID:** SN 13  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Abhisamaya Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0302m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0302m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Doctrinally, *abhisamaya* signifies the "breakthrough" or "penetration" to the four noble truths [Bodhi 2003; Liew 2009]. In the commentary (*Sāratthappakāsinī*), *abhisametāvino* is glossed as abiding having broken through to the noble truths by wisdom (*paññāya ariyasaccāni abhisametvā ṭhitassa*), describing a person endowed with right view (*diṭṭhisampanna*) who has attained stream-entry [Bodhi 2003]. Each sutta in the collection illustrates the momentous spiritual impact of realizing the Dhamma through vivid recurring similes, such as comparing a tiny pinch of dust held on the Buddha's fingernail (*Nakhasikhāsutta*) or droplets of water at the confluence of great rivers with the vast mass of the earth or the ocean; these similes demonstrate that for a noble disciple who has achieved breakthrough, the suffering left to endure is negligible compared to the immeasurable suffering already extinguished [Bodhi 2003; Bodhi 2003_x; Hazra 1994].

- This file contains 12 suttas; 12 of them have known parallels. Full parallels by collection: Pali (12), SĀ (1)
- Examples of full non-Pali parallels: SN 13.11 Tatiyapabbatasutta ↔ SA 439 山

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikāya (2003) — Supplies the structure, English title, translation of the opening fingernail simile, and commentarial glosses on abhisamaya.
- [Bodhi 2003_x] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikāya (2003) — Explains the structural difference between Burmese/PTS editions and the Sinhalese tradition regarding SN 13.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Mentions the teaching of the Abhisamaya Saṁyutta regarding the disciple's past versus remaining suffering.
- [Liew 2009] Liew Jew Chong, The Sarvāstivāda Doctrine of the Path of Spiritual Progress (2009) — Discusses translation terms for abhisamaya ('breakthrough', 'penetrating', Chinese 'immediate-equal').
